name: alerts
description: The ops-triage role: a real 5xx canary rollback, and two alerts whose headline blames the canary but whose own numbers do not support singling it out (docs/adr/0020 §3).

parts.text: Filed the incident and proposed rolling back 0.2.0-waitlist.

hypotheses.cause: the canary build itself is broken
hypotheses.evidence: error_rate canary=1.000 vs stable=0.000, at real traffic

hypotheses.cause: a config only the canary received
hypotheses.evidence: stable on the same window is unaffected

args.reason: error_rate=1.000 on the canary alone, at real traffic, stable unaffected

parts.text: Filed the incident; holding rather than rolling back, since stable fails the same way.

args.title: error_rate 100% on both canary and stable at 5%

hypotheses.cause: a shared dependency is down for every version
hypotheses.evidence: stable error_rate=1.000 too, not just the canary
cannot be distinguished from the shared-dependency cause with stable failing identically

args.reason: stable fails identically; rolling back the canary would not fix an outage that is not canary-specific

parts.text: Filed the incident; holding, since the canary saw no traffic at all this window.

args.title: canary reports no data at 5%, not an observed failure

hypotheses.cause: the canary received no traffic this window
hypotheses.evidence: traffic canary=0.000; error_rate and latency both read 'no data'

hypotheses.cause: a routing problem is keeping traffic off the canary entirely
hypotheses.evidence: zero canary traffic while stable serves normally

args.reason: no canary traffic this window; there is no error rate to roll back on, only an absence of data
